name: epoch-input
title: Epoch Input
description: Reads the value back in the user's zone and UTC, and catches milliseconds pasted as seconds, micro- and nanoseconds, Excel serials, Windows FILETIME, .NET ticks, ISO strings without a zone, date-only strings read as UTC midnight and impossible dates like 30 Feb.

meta.summary: Reads a timestamp back as a date in your zone and UTC and catches unit mix-ups, so a value isn't saved as year 57,754 or the wrong hour.
catches: Excel serial dates, Windows FILETIME and .NET ticks
ISO strings with no time zone, which JavaScript and servers read differently
Date-only strings read as UTC midnight
Impossible dates (30 Feb) and values outside 32-bit range when int32 is set
limits: Unit guesses rely on plausible ranges; very old or far-future dates can be misread
Time zones come from the browser's Intl data
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-invalid and aria-describedby to the readback
After a fix, focus moves to the next fix or back to the input
